interest: This file sheet is intriguing for historians of World War II intelligence and the Japanese diaspora in Latin America, as it illustrates U.S. wartime surveillance of Japanese communities in São Paulo, Brazil. Through the Office of the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs, American officials monitored suspected fifth-column activities and clandestine arming within the Japanese quarter. It also demonstrates State Department classification and filing practices, showing how Latin American intelligence regarding Japanese subjects was indexed and cross-referenced under Far Eastern internal affairs decimal files.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department 'List of Papers' control sheet for decimal file 894.243, categorized under 'Small arms and ammunition, Japan.' The sheet indexes document number 7, a letter dated January 20 from Miller of the Office of the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs reporting on Japanese activities in São Paulo, specifically noting reports of trucks loaded with arms and munitions entering the Japanese quarter. The document notes a cross-reference directing researchers to file 894.20222/78.

The recorded entry is a letter dated January 20 from Miller of the Office of the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs regarding Japanese activities in São Paulo. The entry advises of trucks loaded with arms and munitions entering the Japanese quarter and cross-references decimal file 894.20222/78.
